However, fact that he still appeared to be Director of corporate debtor and Adjudicating Authority had accepted material pointed out by said Director, which was found to be relevant, no interference was warranted - Further, claim of appellants denying signatures in subordination agreement was not necessary for Adjudicating Authority to decide in proceeding under section 7 - It was found that Adjudicating Authority had after considering record found that there was material in form of MOU and agreement which dealt with interest free unsecured loan and equity shares to be allotted to both parties and concluded that there was no time value of money and that it was not financial debt - Whether therefore, there were no reason to interfere with such findings recorded by Adjudicating Authority - Held, yes [Paras 7 to 9]IBC: Where Adjudicating Authority after considering record found that there was material in form of MOU and agreement which dealt with interest free unsecured loan advanced by financial creditors to corporate debtor and concluded that there was no time value of money and that it was not financial debt, findings recorded by Adjudicating Authority could not have been interfered with

Section 5(8), read with section 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 and rule 3(1)(d) of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy (Application to Adjudicating Authority) Rules, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Whether financial contract as per rule 3(1)(d) of Insolvency and Bankruptcy (Application to Adjudicating Authority) Rules, 2016 is must between corporate debtor and financial creditor for setting out terms of a financial debt including tenure of debt, interest payable and date of repayment - Held, yes - Financial creditor granted financial assistance to corporate debtor - Corporate debtor paid interest on amount disbursed by financial creditor once and thereafter, failed to pay further interest - Financial creditor filed an application under section 7 against corporate debtor - Corporate debtor resisted application on various grounds such as lack of contractual agreement and an unidentified period of loan - NCLT by impugned order admitted application under section 7 and initiated CIRP against corporate debtor - Whether financial creditor failed to establish when debt became due and payable and that corporate debtor had committed default - Held, yes - Whether since there was no agreement of loan and no document was there to stipulate period of repayment, financial creditor had failed to establish that transaction in question was a financial debt and corporate debtor had committed default - Held, yes - Whether thus, Adjudicating Authority had erroneously admitted application under section 7 and impugned order was to be set aside - Held, yes [Paras 22, 26, 27 and 33]IBC : Where financial creditor had granted financial assistance to corporate debtor but there was no agreement of loan, financial creditor had failed to establish that transaction in question was a financial debt and corporate debtor had committed default and, therefore, order of NCLT admitting application filed under section 7 by financial creditor was to be set aside

Section 5(8), read with section 5(7), of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Appellant filed its claim as a financial creditor to Resolution Professional (RP) for an amount advanced to corporate debtor as an earnest money for purpose of purchasing surplus land of corporate debtor - RP vide e-mail replied that funds remitted to corporate debtor were interest free advance and same was to be adjusted against sale consideration for proposed sale of land, which did not fall under category of 'financial debt' - Appellant filed application before NCLT seeking direction to RP to adjudicate its claim, revise list of CoC members, and admit him as CoC member - NCLT dismissed said application on ground that there was no contract between parties for sale of any land and, therefore, earnest money advanced by appellant could not be treated as a 'financial debt' - On appeal, appellant submitted that in annual reports of corporate debtor for financial years 2018-19 and 2019-20 earnest money had been classified as a 'financial debt' and, therefore, appellant's claim deserved to be admitted as a financial debt - It was noted that there was no agreement between parties and disbursement made by appellant to corporate debtor was only a payment, which was to be adjusted in sale of land - Whether since disbursement was not in consideration for time value of money, essential condition for accepting a debt to be financial debt was absent - Held, yes - Whether acknowledging liability of earnest money in annual return as financial debt was not akin to admitting same as a financial debt - Held, yes [Paras 18, 19 and 20]IBC : Where appellant had disbursed money to corporate debtor only as payment which was to be adjusted in sale of land and same was not in consideration for time value of money, sum disbursed was not financial debt under section 5(8)  IBC : Where CoC in its commercial decision decided not to allocate any amount to other creditors and appellant who was classified as other creditor was not be able to prove any violation of provisions of IBC, resolution plan approved by NCLT did not require any interference

Section 5(8), read with  sections 5(7) and 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Whether as per section 5(8), a financial debt means a debt along with interest, if any, which is disbursed against consideration for time value of money - Held, yes - Appellant was marketing agency and respondent was TV programme/serial producer for telecast in TV channels - Respondent had share in free commercial time (FCT) in TV programs/serials - They entered into a marketing agreement whereby respondent sold rights of entire 'free commercial time' (FCT) available for programme exclusively to appellant-marketing agency for which appellant paid amount to respondent - As per said agreement appellant was to market and sell FCT - In marketing agreements and subsequent correspondence exchanged between appellant and respondent, no way it was mentioned that amount paid by appellant was to be repayable along with interest over a period of time - Whether since appellant had not disbursed money against consideration for time value of money, clam of appellant was not to be a financial debt within meaning of section 5(8) - Held, yes [Para 21]IBC: Where a marketing agency, appellant, paid amount under marketing agreement to TV programme/Serial producer in lieu of rights of 'free commercial time' (FCT), since there was no clause that amount paid by appellant was to be repayable along with interest over a period of time, same would not be give rise to financial debt

Section 5(8), read with sections 5(7) and 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Appellant entered into Letter of Intent (LoI) for disbursing advance for marketing/financial requirements of development project to be undertaken by respondent corporate debtor - Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) was also enclosed containing terms and conditions and manner of advance to be made by appellant for development of property of corporate debtor - In pursuance of said letter, appellant had advanced different amounts to corporate debtor totalling Rs. 41.75 crores - Corporate debtor sent a letter denying signing and executing MoU - It was also alleged that appellant had failed to raise required funds as promised - Appellant filed a Commercial Suit for recovery wherein an interim injunction order was issued expressing opinion that there was a clear admission of liability - Thereafter, an application was filed under section 7 by appellant claiming as financial creditor for recovery of amount of Rs. 41.75 crores together with interest accrued thereon at rate of 18 per cent - Adjudicating Authority rejected application filed under section 7, holding that arrangement between parties was in nature of business sharing and there was no 'financial debt' - However, on consideration of documents and correspondences, including balance sheets, it was evident that amount paid to corporate debtor as advance for marketing/financial requirements of development project undertaken by corporate debtor was nothing but a financial debt within meaning of IBC - Whether therefore, Adjudicating Authority committed error in holding that appellant was not a financial creditor and rejecting application filed by appellant under section 7 - Held, yes [Paras 19, 21 and 25]IBC : Where on consideration of documents and correspondences, including balance sheets, it was evident that amount paid to corporate debtor as advance for marketing/financial requirements of development project undertaken by corporate debtor was nothing but a financial debt, Adjudicating Authority committed error in holding that appellant was not a 'financial creditor'  IBC : There being acknowledgement of debt in balance sheet, there shall be fresh period of limitation on each acknowledgement, thereby, attracting provisions of section 18 of limitation Act, 1963

Section 5(8), read with sections 7 and 60, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process - Financial debt - Petitioner-financial creditor issued a demand notice against respondent-corporate debtor alleging that he had provided an unsecured loan to respondent, which respondent failed to repay - In reply to said notice, respondent submitted that petitioner had transferred said amount with an intention to buy 25 per cent equity in corporate debtor's development project - On default in making re-payment, petitioner filed a petition under section 7 against respondent - Whether an investment could not be equated with a loan and a sum of money invested with an intention to acquire equity stake or some other interest in company could not be referred as a financial debt - Held, yes - Whether since petitioner had made payment with an intention to acquire 25 per cent equity in corporate debtor's project, said transaction could not be classified as financial debt and, therefore, petition filed under section 7 for initiation of CIRP against corporate debtor was to be dismissed - Held, yes [Paras 21, 28 and 29]IBC : Where petitioner-financial creditor had made payment with an intention to buy 25 per cent equity stake in corporate debtor's development project, money had been invested with an intention to acquire equity stake or some other interest and, therefore, same could not be classified as a financial debt under section 5(8)

Section 5(7), read with sections 5(8) and 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial creditor - Applicant had advanced a loan to respondent corporate debtor - However, corporate debtor failed to repay debt and applicant claiming to be financial creditor filed petition under section 7 against corporate debtor - Whether since neither any loan agreement had been placed on record nor there was any supporting evidence/document to establish applicable rate of interest to be paid on said loan, applicant had failed to prove that loan was disbursed against consideration for time value of money, particularly when respondent company had affirmed that no interest had been paid nor payable at any point of time - Held, yes - Whether therefore, neither instant claim could be termed to be a 'financial debt' nor did applicant come within meaning of 'financial creditor' - Held, yes - Whether since applicant did not come within meaning of 'financial creditor', he became ineligible to file application under section 7 and, therefore, petition filed under section 7 was to be dismissed as not maintainable - Held, yes [Paras 25, 28 and 29]IBC : Where loan was disbursed to corporate debtor without applicable rate of interest, loan was not against consideration for time value of money and could not be considered as financial debt and, hence, applicant who had disbursed such loan was not financial creditor to be eligible to file petition under section 7

I. Section 5(8), read with section  7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Whether amount paid towards purchase of equity in corporate debtor does not constitute a financial debt - Held, yes - Appellant, financial creditor, was one of directors of respondent-corporate debtor - He claimed to have raised loan from a financial institution in his personal name and transferred same to corporate debtor for business purpose - Corporate debtor, however failed to repay loan and interest thereon to appellant - Corporate debtor however submitted that there had been misappropriation of funds from company by appellant and that two criminal complaints were filed against appellant and his accomplices with respect to various crimes committed by them against company - Whether there was nothing on record to show if any decision was taken in Board or Resolution passed to raise above alleged loans - Held, yes - Whether, since there was nothing to show that these amounts were given to corporate debtor by financial creditor, which could be termed as 'disbursement of an amount for time value for money', alleged amount could not be termed as 'financial debt' - Held, yes [Paras 15  16]IBC: Where financial creditor, ex-director of corporate debtor, claimed to have advanced loan to corporate debtor since there was nothing on record to show if any decision was taken in Board or Resolution passed to raise above alleged loans from financial creditor, alleged debt could not be termed as 'financial debt'   IBC: Where appellant's claim, debt and default related to financial year 2012-13 onwards, application under section 7 filed on 25-10-2017 was barred by limitation

Section 5(8), read with section 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Applicant advanced Rs. 2.5 crores to respondent under a draft MoU for development of a project - An amount of Rs. 1.5 crore was admittedly returned - MoUs proposed between applicant and R1 were only draft documents and there was no document or agreement which showed terms on which money was given, nor did it specifically showed whether any interest or consideration against time value for money was payable - Further, there was no repayment schedule - Whether advance paid by applicant to R1 would have no commercial effect of borrowing and same was not financial debt - Held, yes - Whether, thus, CIRP petition was to be dismissed - Held, yes [Para 7]IBC: Where advance was paid and there was no document or agreement which showed terms of payment of any interest or consideration against time value for money, same was not a financial debt

Section 42 of the Companies Act, 2013 read with sections 5(8) and 7 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Private placement - Offer or invitation for subscription of securities on - Appellant transferred an amount of Rs. 2.60 crores to corporate debtor - E-mails were exchanged between parties for execution of MoU, however, no concluded contract was executed - Appellant sent legal notices to corporate debtor asking for repayment including interest - Corporate debtor in a reply stated that appellant never gave any advance or loan to them - Thereafter, appellant filed an application under section 7 of IBC claiming amount as financial debt but same was dismissed by NCLT on ground that appellant failed to prove said financial debt - Appellant submitted that funds given were for share allotment and unsecured loan, and due to non-allotment of shares, amount was repayable under section 42(6) with interest - It was noted that corporate debtor did not issue any private placement offer in pursuance of which appellant made any application of allotment of shares i.e., amount advanced by appellant could not be treated in response of private placement and, hence, said amount could not be related to section 42 - Whether advanced amount was not towards any private placement - Held, yes - Whether since. there was no consideration for time value of money - Held, yes - Whether since, said amount could not be treated as financial debt - Held, yes [Para 20]COMPANY LAW : Where appellant transferred certain sum to corporate debtor claiming it for share allotment and unsecured loan, since no evidence of a private placement offer or share allotment was found and there was no consideration for time value of money, NCLT's dismissal of section 7 application filed by appellant was to be upheld as said amount could not be treated as financial debt  IBC : Where appellant sought repayment of a sum from corporate debtor and NCLT vide impugned order held that no debt was due as said amount was to be adjusted by sale of summit units between parties, since corporate debtor propounded a new theory for repayment and there was lack of records to indicate that Rs. 2.6 crore was paid to appellant, findings of NCLT were to be removed and repayment issue was to be addressed in separate legal proceedings

Section 42 of the Companies Act, 2013 read with sections 5(8) and 7 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Private placement - Offer or invitation for subscription of securities on - Appellant transferred an amount of Rs. 2.60 crores to corporate debtor - E-mails were exchanged between parties for execution of MoU, however, no concluded contract was executed - Appellant sent legal notices to corporate debtor asking for repayment including interest - Corporate debtor in a reply stated that appellant never gave any advance or loan to them - Thereafter, appellant filed an application under section 7 of IBC claiming amount as financial debt but same was dismissed by NCLT on ground that appellant failed to prove said financial debt - Appellant submitted that funds given were for share allotment and unsecured loan, and due to non-allotment of shares, amount was repayable under section 42(6) with interest - It was noted that corporate debtor did not issue any private placement offer in pursuance of which appellant made any application of allotment of shares i.e., amount advanced by appellant could not be treated in response of private placement and, hence, said amount could not be related to section 42 - Whether advanced amount was not towards any private placement - Held, yes - Whether since. there was no consideration for time value of money - Held, yes - Whether since, said amount could not be treated as financial debt - Held, yes [Para 20]  Section 5(8), read with section 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Appellant transferred an amount of Rs. 2.60 crores to corporate debtor - Thereafter, appellant sent legal notices to corporate debtor asking for repayment including interest - Corporate debtor in a reply stated that appellant never gave any advance or loan to them - Thereafter, appellant filed a section 7 application claiming amount as financial debt but same was dismissed by NCLT - In view of an e-mail between parties, NCLT held that no amount was outstanding as said Rs. 2.60 crores was to be adjusted by sale of summit units - Appellant submitted that NCLT's findings that no debt was due was incorrect and without any basis - It was noted that corporate debtor did not support NCLT findings of amount being paid from sale of summit units and propounded a new theory about repayment - Whether since there was lack of record to indicate that Rs. 2.6 crores was paid to appellant, said findings of NCLT were to be removed - Held yes - Whether thus, said issue was to be dealt separately and decided in appropriate proceedings in accordance with law - Held, yes [Para 15]

Section 5(8), read with section 238A, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Corporate debtor entered into a Development Agreement with financial creditor, in which financial creditor was required to provide a refundable Security Deposit of Rs. 12 crores, with an option to add Rs. 3 crores more - In said agreement, additional amount (up to Rs. 3.5 crores) would bear 18 percent interest, payable quarterly - However, due to non-development, financial creditor filed a section 7 application claiming financial debt and highlighted corporate debtor's default in paying interest on Rs. 3.5 crores - Corporate debtor stated that no financial debt existed and that financial creditor was a related party holding 40 per cent equity - However, NCLT admitted said application - Aggrieved by NCLT's order, appellant-suspended director of corporate debtor filed instant appeal - It was noted that letter issued by corporate debtor to financial creditor clearly indicated that advance made over and above security deposit carried interest at a rate of 18 per cent per annum, which was compoundable and payable quarterly - Whether since payment of 18 per cent interest compoundable and payable quarterly clearly indicated time value of money, said transaction would fall within ambit of financial debt under section 5(8) - Held, yes - Whether corporate debtor had acknowledged in its financial statements, amount of interest as a long-term borrowing and had referred to same as loan from financial creditor and, thus, financial creditor had been able to prove debt and default - Held, yes - Whether therefore, NCLT did not commit any error in admitting section 7 application - Held, yes [Paras 28, 29 and 30]IBC : Where letter issued by corporate debtor to a financial creditor clearly showed that an advance made beyond a security deposit by financial creditor carried interest, which was compoundable and payable quarterly and, corporate debtor had acknowledged this interest in its financial statements as a long-term borrowing, referring to it as a loan, financial creditor had proved debt and default and, therefore, NCLT did not commit any error in admitting section 7 application  IBC : Where corporate debtor had acknowledged interest in books of account on 1-4-2013 and thereafter acknowledged that interest was due in financial statements for financial years 2013 to 2018 application filed under section 7 against corporate debtor on 30-9-2019 was within limitation period

Section 5(8), read with section  7 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Applicant granted loan facilities to respondent - On account of respondent's failure to repay loan, instant application was filed under section 7 - Respondent raised a plea that there was no document on record evidencing loan - It was, however, found that sufficient documents like Bill of Exchange, post-dated cheques etc. were produced by applicant - Further, respondent's submission that post-dated cheques were given only for security purpose could not be accepted in view of fact that respondent was paying interest to applicant and, thus, debt was a financial debt as defined under section 5(8) - Whether, on facts, there existed financial debt which respondent failed to discharge and, thus, instant application was to be admitted - Held, yes [Para 5]

Section 5(21), read with section 7 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Operational debt - A Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) was entered between parties with regard to inter-corporate loan facility rendered by financial creditor to corporate debtor - MOU executed between parties provided for payment of interest - Whether requirements of time value of money, as per code, was satisfied and, thus, debt due would be a financial debt - Held, yes - Whether initiation of CIRP against corporate debtor was to be admitted on non-payment of financial debt - Held, yes [Para 10]IBC : Once MOU executed between parties provided for payments of interest, requirements of time value of money, as per Code, was satisfied to make debt due a financial debt  IBC : Where MOU dated 2-5-2015 was signed, according to which corporate debtor would repay financial assistance taken from financial creditors as and when recalled by financial creditor, loans being recalled on 11-7-2017, CIRP petition filed on 16-3-2018 could not be said to be barred by limitation

Section 5(8), read with section  7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Petitioner, a non banking financial corporation, granted financial assistance to corporate debtor - As corporate debtor failed to service interest, said loan was recalled by petitioner - Corporate debtor had neither liquidated outstanding liability nor reduced same - Instant application was filed under section 7 against corporate debtor - Corporate debtor contended that application filed by petitioner was based on contractual agreement, an undefined period of loan etc. and said financial transaction did not tantamount to financial claim - It was noted that petitioner was in business of NBFC to grant financial assistance on interest - Though it was confirmed by petitioner that no agreement was executed, however same was not mandated in cases pertaining to NBFC's - Further grant of financial assistance was evidenced by banking transaction and deduction of TDS duly deposited with Income-tax Authority and substantiated by form 26AS of petitioner - Whether insistence of corporate debtor that transaction was not a financial debt was inexplicable and defence was frivolously raised in a desperate attempt to resist initiation of CIR process - Held, yes - Whether since petitioner was entitled to seek initiation of CIR process of corporate debtor for its inability to liquidate its dues, CIRP was to be admitted - Held, yes [Para 11]IBC : Where corporate debtor failed to liquidate outstanding liability towards petitioner and contended that CIR petition was based on contractual agreement and undefined period of loan etc., since same was not mandatory in case of NBFC's, contention of corporate debtor was inexplicible and CIRP was to be admitted

Section 5(8), read with sections 3(12) and 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 and rule 4 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy (Application to Adjudicating Authority) Rules, 2016 - Financial debt - Applicants claimed to be financial creditors filed instant application under section 7 on ground that respondent company had committed default in making repayment of loan of Rs. 1.20 crores, to it which included interest - In said connection, applicants filed copy of their bank account statements showing advances made by them and audited balance sheet of respondent reflecting loan amount under heading 'Unsecured Loan' - Applicants also filed their income tax returns wherein payment of TDS on interest by respondent on behalf of applicants was reflected and thus, it pointed towards fact that money was taken by respondent against consideration for time value of money - On other hand, respondent claimed that amount was advanced by applicants as contribution to capital and thus, was not a financial debt and categorization of same under head 'unsecured loan' in balance sheet would not change its nature - However, it failed to explain why amount claimed to have been taken as contribution was treated as unsecured loan - Whether thus, 'financial debt' was owed to applicants by respondents - Held, yes - Whether further, when no date had been fixed for repayment of financial debt, it would be repayable on demand and since, in instant case there had been no repayment till date, there was default in repayment of financial debt - Held, yes - Whether therefore, instant application under section 7 against respondent company was to be admitted - Held, yes [Para 17]IBC: Where claim of corporate debtor company was that amount advanced by applicant to it was capital contribution, but same was reflected in balance sheet as unsecured loan, same was to be held as 'financial debt', on default in repayment of which insolvency proceedings was to be initiated

Section 5(8), read with sections 7 and 238A, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Applicant-financial creditor allegedly advanced financial facility to corporate debtor during 2010-12, against payment of interest to be paid on monthly basis - According to applicant, corporate debtor paid interest for October, 2018 and thereafter did not pay any interest and outstanding debt despite various letters and demand notice - Applicant, therefore, filed petition under section 7 - It was noted that applicant had not produced any record of default and also didn't attach latest and complete copy of financial contract reflecting all amendments and waivers to date and even first agreement to show that applicant entered into an agreement with corporate debtor for providing financial assistance, subject to payment of interest was also not attached - Whether applicant failed to establish that amount claimed by him came under definition of financial debt and applicant was financial creditor - Held, yes - Whether, even if it was presumed that applicant had paid amount lastly in 2012, then in view of article 137 of Limitation Act, in absence of any document to show any specific period within which amount was required to be refunded and in absence of acknowledgement of debt, after expiry of 3 years, debt as claimed by applicant was barred by limitation and, therefore, application under section 7 was to be dismissed - Held, yes [Para 19]IBC: Applicant-financial creditor, having failed to produce agreement with corporate debtor for providing financial assistance subject to payment of interest and any record of default made by corporate debtor, application filed by financial creditor under section 7 was not maintainable

Section 5(8), read with section 5(7), of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Appellant filed its claim as a financial creditor to Resolution Professional (RP) for an amount advanced to corporate debtor as an earnest money for purpose of purchasing surplus land of corporate debtor - RP vide e-mail replied that funds remitted to corporate debtor were interest free advance and same was to be adjusted against sale consideration for proposed sale of land, which did not fall under category of 'financial debt' - Appellant filed application before NCLT seeking direction to RP to adjudicate its claim, revise list of CoC members, and admit him as CoC member - NCLT dismissed said application on ground that there was no contract between parties for sale of any land and, therefore, earnest money advanced by appellant could not be treated as a 'financial debt' - On appeal, appellant submitted that in annual reports of corporate debtor for financial years 2018-19 and 2019-20 earnest money had been classified as a 'financial debt' and, therefore, appellant's claim deserved to be admitted as a financial debt - It was noted that there was no agreement between parties and disbursement made by appellant to corporate debtor was only a payment, which was to be adjusted in sale of land - Whether since disbursement was not in consideration for time value of money, essential condition for accepting a debt to be financial debt was absent - Held, yes - Whether acknowledging liability of earnest money in annual return as financial debt was not akin to admitting same as a financial debt - Held, yes [Paras 18, 19 and 20]  Section 31, read with section 30, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Resolution plan - Approval of - Whether where appellant’s claim was classified as other creditor and CoC in its commercial decision decided not to allocate any amount to other creditors and appellant failed to prove any violation of provisions of IBC, resolution plan approved by NCLT did not require any interference - Held, yes [Para 25]

Section 5(8), read with section 238A, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Corporate debtor entered into a Development Agreement with financial creditor, in which financial creditor was required to provide a refundable Security Deposit of Rs. 12 crores, with an option to add Rs. 3 crores more - In said agreement, additional amount (up to Rs. 3.5 crores) would bear 18 percent interest, payable quarterly - However, due to non-development, financial creditor filed a section 7 application claiming financial debt and highlighted corporate debtor's default in paying interest on Rs. 3.5 crores - Corporate debtor stated that no financial debt existed and that financial creditor was a related party holding 40 per cent equity - However, NCLT admitted said application - Aggrieved by NCLT's order, appellant-suspended director of corporate debtor filed instant appeal - It was noted that letter issued by corporate debtor to financial creditor clearly indicated that advance made over and above security deposit carried interest at a rate of 18 per cent per annum, which was compoundable and payable quarterly - Whether since payment of 18 per cent interest compoundable and payable quarterly clearly indicated time value of money, said transaction would fall within ambit of financial debt under section 5(8) - Held, yes - Whether corporate debtor had acknowledged in its financial statements, amount of interest as a long-term borrowing and had referred to same as loan from financial creditor and, thus, financial creditor had been able to prove debt and default - Held, yes - Whether therefore, NCLT did not commit any error in admitting section 7 application - Held, yes [Paras 28, 29 and 30]  Section 238A of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Limitation period - Whether where corporate debtor had acknowledged, interest in books of account on 1-4-2013 and thereafter acknowledged that interest was due in financial statements for financial years 2013 to 2018, application filed on 30-9-2019 was within limitation period - Held, yes [Para 28]

Section 5(8) of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Whether for any creditor to become financial creditor under section 5(7), there must be a financial debt which is owed to that person and such a person can either be principal creditor to whom financial debt is owed or may be a legal assignee to whom such debt has been transferred - Held, yes - Corporate debtor was a wholly owned subsidiary of IIL - Corporate debtor had approached IIL for financial assistance, which was provided - Meanwhile, liquidation proceedings commenced against IIL and liquidator published Process Memorandum, wherein amount defaulted by corporate debtor was recorded as Rs. 5.10 crores - Appellant-financial creditor had bid for assets/receivables of IIL and entered into a Deed of Assignment with Liquidator of IIL whereby assets of IIL were transferred in favour of financial creditor - Subsequently, financial creditor issued a legal notice and filed a section 7 application against corporate debtor before NCLT, which was rejected by NCLT on ground that debt and default did not exist - It was noted that Deed of Assignment showed that 'receivables' of IIL were assigned a sum of Rs. 25 lakh only on an 'as is where is', 'as is what is' and 'whatever there is' and 'no recourse' basis and Annual Report of IIL for financial year 2015-16 had shown sum given to corporate debtor under Head of 'Receivables' and not under Head of 'Intercorporate Loan', which should have been treatment, if amount was a loan - Whether since assigned amount had been clearly shown as trade receivable in Deed of Assignment, it could not be viewed as a loan particularly when there was no contract/agreement between corporate debtor and IIL recording advance of any loan - Held, yes - Whether there was nothing placed on record by appellant to substantiate that disbursement had been made for consideration for time value of money and, thus, NCLT did not commit any error in rejecting section 7 application filed by appellant - Held, yes [Paras 14, 25 and 26]IBC : Where appellant-financial creditor filed a section 7 application against corporate debtor on basis of a Deed of Assignment, where sum given to corporate debtor by IIL was transferred to appellant, however, said sum was clearly shown as a trade receivable rather than a loan and there was no contract or agreement between corporate debtor and IIL designating sum given as a loan, NCLT did not commit any error in rejecting section 7 application filed by appellant against corporate debtor

Section 5(8), read with section 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Appellant-financial creditor advanced loan of Rs. 1 crore to respondent, a real estate company for construction of a project 'Madina Heights' - Respondent assured to repay loan with interest @ 18 per cent per annum besides offering 15 per cent share in profit of project - However, respondent failed to repay loan - Appellant issued demand notice - Since payments were still not forthcoming from respondent, appellant filed a section 7 petition seeking admission of respondent into corporate insolvency resolution process which was rejected by Adjudicating Authority as non-maintainable - It was an admitted fact that there was no written contract or agreement between appellant and respondent governing terms and conditions by which sum was advanced by appellant and disbursed to account of respondent - Whether since appellant had failed to muster clinching proof and evidence in terms of financial records to show that sum advanced by them was indisputably interest-bearing and that interest had continued to accrue and was being realized as consideration for time value of money, sum advanced by appellant to respondent did not satisfy ingredients of financial debt of disbursal, time value of money and commercial effect of borrowing - Held, yes - Whether further said project was still in progress and compliances, both procedural and regulatory, were still pending and hence no occasion for default could be said to have occurred as debt was not due or payable - Held, yes - Whether thus, debt and default not having been clearly established, there was no infirmity in impugned order rejecting Section 7 application - Held, yes [Paras 21, 25, 26 and 27]IBC : Where financial creditor had failed to muster clinching proof and evidence in terms of financial records to show that sum advanced by them to corporate debtor was indisputably interest-bearing and that interest had continued to accrue and was being realized as consideration for time value of money, sum advanced by financial creditor to corporate debtor did not satisfy ingredients of financial debt of disbursal, time value of money and commercial effect of borrowing, and thus, instant section 7 petition by financial creditor was to be dismissed

Section 5(8) of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Whether for any creditor to become financial creditor under section 5(7), there must be a financial debt which is owed to that person and such a person can either be principal creditor to whom financial debt is owed or may be a legal assignee to whom such debt has been transferred - Held, yes - Corporate debtor was a wholly owned subsidiary of IIL - Corporate debtor had approached IIL for financial assistance, which was provided - Meanwhile, liquidation proceedings commenced against IIL and liquidator published Process Memorandum, wherein amount defaulted by corporate debtor was recorded as Rs. 5.10 crores - Appellant-financial creditor had bid for assets/receivables of IIL and entered into a Deed of Assignment with Liquidator of IIL whereby assets of IIL were transferred in favour of financial creditor - Subsequently, financial creditor issued a legal notice and filed a section 7 application against corporate debtor before NCLT, which was rejected by NCLT on ground that debt and default did not exist - It was noted that Deed of Assignment showed that 'receivables' of IIL were assigned a sum of Rs. 25 lakh only on an 'as is where is', 'as is what is' and 'whatever there is' and 'no recourse' basis and Annual Report of IIL for financial year 2015-16 had shown sum given to corporate debtor under Head of 'Receivables' and not under Head of 'Intercorporate Loan', which should have been treatment, if amount was a loan - Whether since assigned amount had been clearly shown as trade receivable in Deed of Assignment, it could not be viewed as a loan particularly when there was no contract/agreement between corporate debtor and IIL recording advance of any loan - Held, yes - Whether there was nothing placed on record by appellant to substantiate that disbursement had been made for consideration for time value of money and, thus, NCLT did not commit any error in rejecting section 7 application filed by appellant - Held, yes [Paras 14, 25 and 26]

Section 5(8), read with sections 7 and 60, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process - Financial debt - Petitioner-financial creditor issued a demand notice against respondent-corporate debtor alleging that he had provided an unsecured loan to respondent, which respondent failed to repay - In reply to said notice, respondent submitted that petitioner had transferred said amount with an intention to buy 25 per cent equity in corporate debtor's development project - On default in making re-payment, petitioner filed a petition under section 7 against respondent - Whether an investment could not be equated with a loan and a sum of money invested with an intention to acquire equity stake or some other interest in company could not be referred as a financial debt - Held, yes - Whether since petitioner had made payment with an intention to acquire 25 per cent equity in corporate debtor's project, said transaction could not be classified as financial debt and, therefore, petition filed under section 7 for initiation of CIRP against corporate debtor was to be dismissed - Held, yes [Paras 21, 28 and 29]

Section 5(8), read with section 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Corporate debtor borrowed loan against payment of interest as agreed between parties - Loan was disbursed against consideration for time value of money with a clear commercial effect of borrowing - Moreover debt claimed in application for initiating CIRP included both component of outstanding principal and interest - Whether not only claim would come within purview of 'financial debt' but also applicant could clearly be termed as 'financial creditor' so as to prefer application under section 7 - Held, yes [Para 20]IBC : Where under a loan agreement, corporate debtor borrowed loan against payment of interest, creditor's claim would fall within purview of financial debt  IBC : Where in a recovery suit against corporate debtor, decree was passed in 2013, but even after lapse of more than five years of passing such decree, corporate debtor had not paid its pending dues, instant application for CIRP filed in 2018 being within limitation period of 12 years was to be admitted

Section 5(8), read with section 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Corporate debtor availed a cash loan from financial creditor /applicant - Corporate debtor failed to repay said loan and thus, applicant filed instant petition under section 7 - In order to prove financial debt, applicant produced copy of promissory note signed by Director of corporate debtor - On perusal of promissory note, it was found that it did not contain any terms regarding repayment of amount with interest and said promissory note was not duly stamped - Whether promissory note comes under purview of section 2(22) of Indian Stamp Act and same was liable to stamp duty - Held, yes - Whether since there were no terms stipulated in promissory note that corporate debtor was liable to repay amount with interest, said promissory note could not acquire status of financial debt and same could not be considered to be disbursed against consideration for time value of money - Held, yes - Whether therefore, instant petition was to be rejected - Held, yes [Paras 30 and 35]

I. Section 5(8), read with section 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Whether section 5(8) makes condition of interest optional by using words 'if any' as suffix to word 'interest' in main clause - Held, yes - Whether interest-free loan results into economic advantage to borrower and, hence, time value of money exists in case of interest-free loan as well and application filed under section 7 can be admitted in case of interest-free loan - Held, yes - Whether status of financial creditor as shareholder/director of company is a disqualification to file application under section 7 - Held, no [Para 7]IBC : Time value of money exists in case of interest free loan as well and same will be considered as financial debt for filing CIRP under section 7  IBC : Where loan sanctioned by financial creditor to corporate debtor was repayable after six months, limitation to file petition under section 7 would start after six months from disbursement of loan and not immediately on disbursement

Section 5(8), read with section 10, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Applicant/corporate debtor obtained financial assistance from various sources - Due to inability of applicant to repay said debts, instant application was filed under section 10 - In order to prove financial debt, applicant/corporate debtor attached copies of various inter-corporate deposit agreements entered between corporate debtor and other parties - As per terms and conditions of said agreement, there was neither any fixed date for repayment nor any fixed rate of interest - Whether in terms of section 5(8), any contract/agreement providing money, whose consideration is 'time value of money' will qualify definition of 'financial debt' - Held, yes - Whether, since in Inter-Corporate Deposits Agreements there was no date of repayment and no rate of interest, price associated with length of time that an investor must wait until an investment would mature or related income was earned could not be calculated; only fact that some amount was outstanding and that was to be paid would not qualify criteria of "time value of money" and, hence claim made by Applicant could not be treated as "Financial Debt" - Held, yes - Whether, therefore, claim raised by applicant could not be treated as 'financial debt' and, as a consequence, instant application was to be rejected - Held, yes [Paras 8 and 15]

Section 7 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Initiation by financial creditor - With a view to set up a plant, all shareholders of corporate debtor company including applicant had given interest free unsecured loan to be used as margin money to enabling company to get loan facility from bank - Applicant admitted that unsecured loan would be subordinate to claim made by bank and agreed not to seek recovery of his unsecured loan till liability of bank stood extinguished - Corporate debtor failed to repay - Thus, applicant initiated insolvency resolution process against company - However, corporate debtor submitted that amount being claimed was not a loan in terms of financial debt, nor was there any agreement to pay interest on such loan and that said loan amount was not repayable on demand as it was part of working capital for procuring financial assistance from bank - Further, principal money lender i.e. Bank had not made any claim - Whether, instant insolvency resolution process could not be admitted - Held, yes [Para 9]Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code: Where promoter of company had given interest free unsecured loan to company to be used as margin money enabling it to get loan facility from bank which became part of company's working capital and further promoter agreed not to seek recovery till liability of bank stood extinguished, on company's failure to repay, promoter could not initiated insolvency resolution process

Section 5(8) of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Corporate debtor had been incurring losses and defaulted in re-payment of loan - Financial creditor as a prospective investor came out to take charge and run corporate debtor company - As per terms of MoU, financial creditor brought in funds from time to time for corporate debtor's working capital, cleared its liabilities and paid other expenses - However, corporate debtor did not perform its obligation to proceed to negotiate terms of definitive agreement as envisaged for implementation of provisions of MoU - Therefore, money infused by financial creditor was demanded back which corporate debtor failed to pay - Whether since money brought by financial creditor into corporate debtor company was part of purchase agreement for purchase of corporate debtor in terms of MoU, which did not happen, amount raised fell within purview of financial debt - Held, yes [Para 19]IBC: Where money brought by financial creditor into corporate debtor company was part of Agreement for purchase of corporate debtor company, but said purchase did not happen, amount raised by financial creditor would fall within purview of financial debt  IBC: Where financial creditor made payment in 2014 and Whatsapp messages were exchanged till 2016, through which corporate debtor assured to make payment, CIRP application filed in 2018, being within limitation period of 3 years, was to be admitted

Section 5(8), read with sections 3(12) and 5(7), of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Appellant had given unsecured loan facility to respondent-corporate debtor - Corporate debtor had been paying interest on unsecured loan and also had been deducting and depositing Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) on interest paid to appellant - Corporate debtor defaulted in payment of unsecured loan - Appellant issued demand notice to corporate debtor seeking repayment of unpaid financial debt - Appellant filed application under section 7 for initiation of CIRP against corporate debtor - NCLT by impugned order rejected said application holding that appellant had failed to establish that unsecured loan he had granted fell within scope of financial debt in absence of any loan agreement setting out terms and conditions of agreement - Whether there were no documents/records to prove that appellant was financial creditor - Held, yes - Whether audited balance sheet also did not prove existence of financial debt and default as defined under section 3(12) - Held, yes - Whether since there was no financial debt and default as proved by appellant, NCLT had rightly rejected application filed by appellant under section 7 - Held, yes [Paras 16 and 17]IBC : Where appellant - financial creditor had given unsecured loan to corporate debtor but failed to prove existence of financial debt and default, NCLT had rightly rejected application filed by appellant under section 7 for initiation of CIRP against corporate debtor

Section 5(8), read with section 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Applicant-financial creditor was in management of corporate debtor which had taken a loan from SBI - Later, management of corporate debtor was transferred to 'B' - Applicant filed application under section 7 against corporate debtor alleging that corporate debtor defaulted in repaying unsecured loan taken from applicant - Whether since terms and conditions of loan agreement with SBI of which applicant was party provided that unsecured loan made available by applicant to corporate debtor did not become due for payment till bank loan was fully liquidated i.e., on 16-2-2018, application filed on 3-7-2015 claiming that corporate debtor owed an amount to applicant was pre-matured and not maintainable - Held, yes - Whether since applicant had failed to bring on record any evidence to suggest that he disbursed money against consideration for time value of money and there was no information about rate of interest on principal amount, loan did not satisfy requirement of financial debt as contemplated under section 5(8) - Held, yes - Whether thus, applicant failed to show that corporate debtor owed an amount and there was a default in payment of such debt and, therefore, application under section 7 was to be dismissed - Held, yes [Paras 39, 40, 43, 44, 57 and 58]IB Code: Where applicant had failed to bring on record any evidence to suggest that he disbursed money against consideration for time value of money and there was no information about rate of interest on principal amount, loan did not satisfy requirement of financial debt as contemplated under section 5(8)

Section 5(8), read with section 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Applicant's case was that he had given a loan of Rs. 35 lakhs to respondent company through one of its directors namely 'S' - On account of failure of respondent to repay loan amount along with interest as per agreed terms instant application was filed under section 7 - Respondent raised an objection that applicant was not a financial creditor and debt claimed by him was not a financial debt in terms of section 5(8)(a) - It was further submitted that receipts evidencing payment of money was unstamped documents and, therefore, inadmissible in law - It was noted that letter of acknowledgement of debt relied upon by applicant did not bear seal of respondent company, seal of directors and it was not even supported with any resolution of Board of Directors of respondent company - Moreover, there was no evidence on record showing that Board of Directors of respondent company had passed a resolution authorising director 'S' to take loan on its behalf or acknowledge liability - Whether on facts, applicant failed to prove that respondent had borrowed money with a liability to pay interest as referred to in letter of acknowledgement - Held, yes - Whether, therefore, there being no financial debt in existence, instant application deserved to be dismissed - Held, yes [Paras 12 and 15]IBC : Where applicant filed application under section 7 on account of failure of respondent company to repay its debt, in view of fact that letter of acknowledgement of debt relied upon by applicant did not bear seal of respondent company, seal of directors and it was not even supported with any resolution of Board of Directors of respondent company, instant application deserved to be dismissed  IBC : In case of financial debt, when financial creditor puts a date in cheque and presents it in bank and gets it dishonoured, in such a case, said date of dishonour of cheque cannot be accepted as date of default as per section 3(12)

Section 5(8), read with sections 5(6) and 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Financial Creditor's/applicants provided loan facilities to corporate debtor - Corporate debtor committed default in repayment - Thus, applicants filed instant petition under section 7 - In instant petition, corporate debtor alleged that neither any loan was taken, nor payment of interest was payable by corporate debtor to applicants - Whether onus lies on applicants to establish that loan was given against consideration for time value of money and debt claimed comes within purview of financial debt - Held, yes - Whether since applicants had failed to bring on record any evidence to suggest that they had disbursed money to corporate debtor against consideration for time value of money, loan given by applicants would not come within purview of financial debt and applicants could not be treated as financial creditors - Held, yes [Paras 29, 30, 31 and 32]IBC: Where applicants claiming to be financial creditors, failed to prove that they had disbursed money to corporate debtor, against consideration for time value of money, loan, if any, given would not come within purview of financial debt and, thus, applicants were not financial creditors

Section 5(8), read with section 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 and section 42 of the Companies Act, 2013 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Whether refund of Share Application Money, in event of non-allotment of shares attracts interest as provided for under section 42(6) of Companies Act and, therefore, qualifies essential ingredients of section 5(8) in terms of consideration paid for time value of money and falls within definition of ambit of 'Financial Debt' as defined under section 5(8) - Held, yes - Whether where financial creditor was allotted equity shares on preferential basis in lieu of loan but said allotment was revoked by Board resolution, money given by financial creditor indeed falls within definition of Share Application Money and Share Application Money in event of non-allotment of shares, attracts interest under section 42(6) of Companies Act, 2013 and, therefore, falls within ambit of definition of 'Financial Debt' as defined under section 5(8) - Held, yes [Paras 18 and 20]IBC : Refund of share application in event of non-allotment of shares attracts interest under section 42(6) of Companies Act, 2013 and, therefore, falls within ambit of definition of 'Financial Debt' under section 5(8)

Section  5(8),  read with section  7,  of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 -  Corporate insolvency resolution process  - Financial debt - Financial creditor i.e., REL (successor of RAIML) and Corporate Debtor were group companies under common promoters and were related parties during relevant period - Under a one-page MoU between RAIML and Corporate Debtor, an unsecured demand loan up to Rs. 5 crores was sanctioned at 13% interest - Pursuant thereto, Rs. 3.60 crores was credited to Corporate Debtor and, on same day, Corporate Debtor transferred Rs. 3.60 crores to Religare Finvest Ltd. (RFL), a subsidiary of REL - Bank entries for 30-31.03.2009 reflected several similar same-day intra-group receipts and transfers - Similar MoUs were executed in subsequent years - On 08.12.2017, RAIML was amalgamated with REL - REL filed a Section 7 application against Corporate Debtor claiming about Rs. 5.87 crores - Corporate Debtor replied that no legally recognized financial debt existed - Adjudicating Authority admitted Section 7 application - Whether transaction between RAIML with Corporate Debtor by MoU dated 30.03.2009 and subsequent MoUs read with transaction in bank account of Corporate Debtor dated 31.03.2009 did not reflect a financial transaction entitling financial creditor to initiate proceedings under Section 7 against Corporate Debtor - Held, yes - Whether Corporate Debtor having questioned very existence of financial debt in transaction between parties, Adjudicating Authority was required to look into pleadings and material to find out true nature of transaction whereas Adjudicating Authority failed to look into relevant pleas and materials on record and had arrived erroneous finding that there was a financial debt - Held, yes - Whether FIR 50/2019 lodged by Religare Finvest Ltd. subsidiary of financial creditor and allegations made therein and subsequent proceeding in reference to FIR were not to be relied as any substantive evidence in proceeding under Section 7 except fact that such an FIR had been lodged by subsidiary of Financial Creditor making allegations against erstwhile promoter of Corporate Debtor and Financial Creditor - Held, yes - Whether since materials on record clearly proved that there was no financial debt which was disbursed by Financial Creditor to Corporate Debtor for time value of money and transaction of round tripping of money/layering of money for some undisclosed fraudulent purposes there was no financial debt in existence in transaction and its initiation of CIRP by Financial Creditor could not have been made on such transaction - Held, yes - Whether thus, order of Adjudicating Authority admitting Section 7 application could not be sustained - Held, yes [Paras 50 and 51]

Section 5(8), read with  sections 5(7) and 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Whether 'Financial debt' means outstanding principal due in respect of a loan and would also include interest thereon, if any interest were payable thereon; if there is no interest payable on loan, only outstanding principal would qualify as a financial debt - Held, yes - Whether trigger for initiation of Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process by a financial creditor under section 7 is occurrence of a default by corporate debtor - Held, yes - Whether definition of 'Financial Debt' in section 5(8) does not expressly exclude an interest free loan - Held, yes - Whether 'Financial Debt' would have to be construed to include interest free loans advanced to finance business operations of a corporate body - Held, yes - Whether thus, a person who gives a term loan to a corporate person, free of interest, on account of its working capital requirements is a financial creditor, and, therefore, is competent to initiate corporate resolution process under section 7 - Held, yes [Paras 22 and 31]IBC : Definition of 'Financial Debt' in section 5(8) does not expressly exclude an interest free loan; a person who gives a term loan to a corporate person free of interest on account of its working capital requirements is a financial creditor, and, therefore, is competent to initiate Corporate Insolvency resolution process under section 7

Section 5(8), read with section 7 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Respondent was engaged in business of developing, planning, constructing and selling residential  commercial complexes - Applicant and respondent entered into a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) in terms of which applicant paid certain amount to respondent for development of residential complex - As per terms of MOU, in event of respondent's failure to develop residential complex within prescribed time, it had to repay amount paid by applicant along with interest - Applicant's case was that in view of respondent's failure to develop residential complex as per agreed terms, a demand notice was issued to refund amount along with interest - Since respondent did not make payment, instant application was filed under section 7 - Whether in order to bring transaction within definition of 'financial debt', basic requirement is that money was disbursed against consideration of time value of money which did not exist in instant case - Held, yes - Whether, therefore, in absence of any financial debt in existence, application filed under section 7 was to be dismissed - Held, yes [Paras 13 and 21]

Section 5(8), read with section 7 of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Respondent was engaged in business of developing, planning, constructing and selling residential  commercial complexes - Applicant and respondent entered into a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) in terms of which applicant paid certain amount to respondent for development of residential complex - As per terms of MOU, in event of respondent's failure to develop residential complex within prescribed time, it had to repay amount paid by applicant along with interest - Applicant's case was that in view of respondent's failure to develop residential complex as per agreed terms, a demand notice was issued to refund amount along with interest - Since respondent did not make payment, instant application was filed under section 7 - Whether in order to bring transaction within definition of 'financial debt', basic requirement is that money was disbursed against consideration of time value of money which did not exist in instant case - Held, yes - Whether, therefore, in absence of any financial debt in existence, application filed under section 7 was to be dismissed - Held, yes [Paras 13 and 21]

Section 5(8), read with  section 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Applicant sanctioned various loan facilities to respondent - On account of failure of respondent to repay loan as per agreed terms, a notice was issued under section 8 - Respondent did not send any reply to said notice - Applicant thus filed instant application under section 7 - It was undisputed that respondent had taken credit facilities against payment of interest as agreed between parties - Thus, loan was disbursed against consideration of time value of money with a clear commercial effect of borrowing - Whether in view of aforesaid it could be concluded that claim raised by applicant would come within purview of 'financial debt' and applicant bank could be termed as 'financial creditor' - Held, yes - Whether, therefore, when applicant had placed on record voluminous and overwhelming evidence in support of claim as well as default in payment of financial debt, instant application deserved to be admitted - Held, yes [Paras 36 and 42]IB Code : Where applicant sanctioned various loan facilities to respondent on interest basis, in view of failure of respondent to repay said loan alongwith interest, instant application filed under section 7 was to be admitted

Section 5(8) of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - An application filed under section 7 was admitted in case of corporate debtor - Applicant was a shareholder in corporate debtor - Applicant's case was that he had also given loan to corporate debtor under an oral agreement - Applicant submitted his claim before Resolutional Professional - Resolution Professional refused to accept applicant's claim on ground that there was no loan agreement in writing, hence, nature of debt could not be regarded as 'Financial Debt' as defined under section 5(8) - Whether since there was only an alleged oral agreement and, moreover, applicant had not proved that corporate debtor had paid any interest in past, amount in question could not be regarded as 'financial debt' - Held, yes - Whether, therefore, impugned order passed by Resolution Professional did not require any interference - Held, yes [Para 5]

Section 5(8) of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Applicant company which was also under CIRP claimed to have advanced a sum of certain amount as loan to respondent/corporate debtor - It contended that since corporate debtor failed to repay loan amount, same was to be considered as financial debt and accordingly applicant was a financial creditor - It was noted that there was no documentary evidence on record to suggest that amount claimed to have transferred by applicant to corporate debtor were advanced as loan - Balance sheet of applicant had shown certain amount given as loan to others but there was no mention of name of corporate debtor - Besides this, it was an admitted fact that applicant company and corporate debtor were group companies and directors on boards and promoters were common -Thus, money claimed to be financial debt did not change hands as it remained in same hands of directors and promoters who were common in both companies which were undergoing CIR process - Thus, there appeared to be round tripping of money and matter was under investigation of police - Whether, on facts, application filed by financial creditor was to be dismissed - Held, yes [Paras 14 to 17]IBC : Where financial creditor claimed to have advanced loan to corporate debtor, since financial creditor could not place on record any documentary evidence to suggest that amount claimed to have transferred by it to corporate debtor were advanced as loan, alleged loan amount could not be termed as 'financial debt'

Section 5(8), read with section  7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Applicant-financial creditor claimed that it had advanced loan to respondent-corporate debtor - As respondent failed to repay loan, application was filed under section 7 against corporate debtor - It was noted that there was no loan agreement on record and no Board Resolution was placed or produced by applicant company empowering it to grant loan to corporate debtor and only document on strength of which applicant was claiming that debt had arisen out of loan transactions was Form 26AS reflecting credit of interest amount and deduction of TDS - Whether in absence of any loan agreement and relevant Board Resolution, merely on basis of Form 26AS, it could not be presumed that any loan was disbursed by applicant to corporate debtor, which could be treated as the financial debt - Held, yes - Whether since applicant/financial creditor had failed to demonstrate that debt claimed in its application was arising out of any loan transactions and was a financial debt, application under section 7 was to be dismissed - Held, yes [Paras 28 and 33]

Section 5(8), read with section 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process - Financial debt - Corporate debtor availed financial assistance from applicant but committed default in repayment - Thus, applicant filed instant application under section 7 - Corporate debtor raised objections that applicant was neither a financial creditor nor debts claimed by applicant came within purview of financial debt - It also raised a dispute that amount was due and payable at convenience of corporate debtor within a period of seven years and not on demand by applicant - As regard to first objection, it was noted that loan was disbursed against consideration for time value of money with a clear commercial effect of borrowing, thus, not only present claim came within purview of financial debt but also applicant was a financial creditor - As regard to second objection, it was noted that corporate debtor had sent an email to financial creditor in which it had not only accepted its liability but also sought time to repay debt at earliest, therefore, contention of corporate debtor that amount was payable after seven years was baseless and same could not be sustained - Whether since applicant had placed on record documents to prove default in repayment and, moreover, application of applicant was complete and there was no disciplinary proceeding pending against proposed RP, said application was to be admitted - Held, yes [Paras 14, 25, 39 and 40]

Section 5(8), read with section 7, of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Corporate insolvency resolution process - Financial debt - Appellant-financial creditor advanced loan of Rs. 1 crore to respondent, a real estate company for construction of a project 'Madina Heights' - Respondent assured to repay loan with interest @ 18 per cent per annum besides offering 15 per cent share in profit of project - However, respondent failed to repay loan - Appellant issued demand notice - Since payments were still not forthcoming from respondent, appellant filed a section 7 petition seeking admission of respondent into corporate insolvency resolution process which was rejected by Adjudicating Authority as non-maintainable - It was an admitted fact that there was no written contract or agreement between appellant and respondent governing terms and conditions by which sum was advanced by appellant and disbursed to account of respondent - Whether since appellant had failed to muster clinching proof and evidence in terms of financial records to show that sum advanced by them was indisputably interest-bearing and that interest had continued to accrue and was being realized as consideration for time value of money, sum advanced by appellant to respondent did not satisfy ingredients of financial debt of disbursal, time value of money and commercial effect of borrowing - Held, yes - Whether further said project was still in progress and compliances, both procedural and regulatory, were still pending and hence no occasion for default could be said to have occurred as debt was not due or payable - Held, yes - Whether thus, debt and default not having been clearly established, there was no infirmity in impugned order rejecting Section 7 application - Held, yes [Paras 21, 25, 26 and 27]

facts.text:
The corporate debtor, with an intention of setting up a project for the manufacture of flexible packaging material under co-extension process at an estimated cost of Rs.30 crores, had approached Canara Bank for financial assistance. While the said bank sanctioned a term loan of Rs.14.2 crores for construction of the building and purchase of plant and machinery, the promoters of corporate debtor were required to meet the condition of investing the margin money. Accordingly, all six promoters, including the financial creditor, had given interest free unsecured loan to the corporate debtor.

The financial creditor alleged that the corporate debtor failed to take any steps to liquidate or reduce the liability qua him despite various reminders. Thus, he issued demand notice under section 8. In response to the said notice, corporate debtor submitted that the amount being claimed was not a loan in terms of financial debt, nor was there any agreement to pay interest thereon. It was not to be repaid on demand as it was the basis of procuring financial assistance from their bank for establishing the corporate debtor for its working capital. The financial creditor was an equity holder and with a view to set up a plant, all shareholders had paid various amounts as the margin money to enable them to get the loan facility from Canara bank.

■

The appellant was a financial creditor of the corporate debtor(CD). The appellant had advanced an interest free loan to the corporate debtor to discharge the liabilities of the other secured financial creditors. The loan advanced by the appellant did not bear interest and was to be repaid after the settlement of the secured financial loans of the CD under the one time settlement scheme but when the CD failed to repay the loan after settlement of the secured loans, the appellant issued notice and recalled its loan to be repaid within 15 days. The appellant alleged that the amount of loan was reflected in the financial statement of the Respondent as unsecured loan. The corporate debtor failed to repay the loan after settlement of the secured loans.

■

The appellant filed an application under section 7 for the resolution of an interest free loan. The NCLT dismissed the application on ground that amount given by the appellant to the corporate debtor was not a financial debt and, hence, the corporate debtor was not owed to pay the appellant and that the loan was advanced in violation of section 186(2) of the Companies Act, 2013 and, therefore, was void and unforceable.

■

On appeal:

The respondent-corporate debtor sought financial assistance from the appellant-corporate debtor.

The appellant granted an unsecured term loan of Rs. 75 lakhs to the corporate debtor and, by way of RTGS payment of Rs. 50 lakhs, Rs. 5 lakhs and Rs. 20 lakhs were disbursed and, it was agreed between the parties that the repayment of the unsecured term loan will be made on demand.

The corporate debtor deducted tax on the interest amount in the financial year 2017-18. A total amount of Rs. 52.250 thousand was incurred as interest on the principle amount and, the corporate debtor deducted the TDS of Rs. 5250 thousand on 31-3-2018 but, had not paid it to the financial creditor.

The appellant sent a letter to the corporate debtor for the repayment of unsecured loan along with interest within two months and, the board of directors of the appellant had passed resolution to file a case against the corporate debtor in the NCLT.

The application under section 7 was filed by the appellant before the NCLT.

The NCLT directed the appellant to demonstrate that Income Tax for the assessment year 2018-19 had been taken into account and, the TDS deducted was adjusted and credited.

The appellant filed various documents including the Auditor's Report as well as copy of section 194A of the Income-tax Act.

The NCLT by impugned order held that the financial creditor failed to show the nature of the transaction between the parties and that the amount paid did not come under the definition of financial debt and, therefore, application filed by the financial creditor was dismissed.

The appellant filed instant appeal on ground that the NCLT committed error in holding that the appellant had not been able to prove financial debt, however, the documents brought on the record by the appellant including the balance sheets and bank transactions clearly proved the financial debt and, thus, NCLT committed an error in rejecting the application.

The financial creditor granted financial assistance of Rs. 6.10 crores to the corporate debtor.

The corporate debtor paid interest once after deduction of TDS, thereafter, corporate debtor failed to pay further interest. The financial creditor recalled the loan.

The corporate debtor had not liquidated the outstanding liabilities. Hence, the financial creditor filed the application under section 7.

The corporate debtor filed the reply and resisted the application on various grounds inter alia lack of any contractual agreement, an undefined period of loan, absence of any agreement for payment of interest at any specific rate and the said transaction did not fall within the definition of financial debt.

NCLT found no substance in the defence raised by the corporate debtor and held that the transaction does not get vitiated for want of agreement in terms of section 186(ii) of the Companies Act, 2013. NCLT by impugned order admitted the application and initiated CIRP against the corporate debtor.

The appellant, ex-director of corporate debtor, filed instant appeal against the impugned order of NCLT.

The appellant submitted that the Adjudicating Authority failed to appreciate that the financial creditor did not produce any loan agreement or instrument along with its application, and there were no pleadings regarding the basic terms of the alleged financial contract or financial debt including the date of repayment, applicable interest and date of default.

■

The applicant- financial creditor claimed that it had extended a loan to the Corporate Debtor during the period from 13.06.2007 to 27.03.2009. The said loan was extended in his personal capacity and was repayable on demand.

■
